t: This is Metro Central Heights, a Grade II listed group of residential buildings in Walworth, in Southwark. It began as Alexander Fleming House, an office complex designed by the Hungarian-born modernist architect Ernő Goldfinger and built in the early 1960s. The original name honours Sir Alexander Fleming, the Scottish microbiologist who discovered penicillin in 1928, the first antibiotic. He shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for it. Goldfinger's design is what you are looking at now.
